name: Omnicart Global Commerce
tagline: Global e-commerce platform, real-time inventory management, high-conversion checkout, and global fulfillment.
operatingCadence: High-throughput retail sprint cadence with Black Friday load resilience, sub-second checkout SLAs, and strict ETA tracking.

workAreas.name: Executive & Commercial Strategy
workAreas.focus: Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), customer acquisition cost (CAC), return on ad spend (ROAS), supplier relationships, and sales targets.
workAreas.targets: 100% quarterly GMV targets, positive unit economics, customer lifetime value (LTV) >3x CAC.

workAreas.name: E-Commerce Architecture & Payments
workAreas.focus: Distributed cart architecture, multi-currency checkout, payment gateway integrations (Stripe, Adyen, Apple Pay), and initial store exploration.
workAreas.targets: Sub-800ms checkout completion, zero payment double-charge incidents, zero direct coding by leadership.

workAreas.name: Storefront & Fulfillment Management
workAreas.focus: Promotional calendar alignment, backlog ticket decomposition, developer task assignment, mandatory ETA tracking, and active follow-ups.
workAreas.targets: 100% ticket allocation with agreed ETAs, zero promotion launch delays, rigorous sprint velocity.

workAreas.name: Storefront & Inventory Engineering
workAreas.focus: Next.js/React storefront, live stock reservation, cart synchronization, recommendation algorithms, and ERP integrations.
workAreas.targets: 85%+ unit test coverage, sub-100ms inventory lookup queries, delivery within agreed ETAs.

workAreas.name: E-Commerce QA & Load Testing
workAreas.focus: Cart-to-checkout E2E automated tests, payment gateway mock testing, flash sale stress testing (k6), defect reporting, and release gating.
workAreas.targets: Zero checkout funnel regressions, 100,000 concurrent user load test sign-off, detailed bug reports to management.

workAreas.name: Cloud Operations & CDN Infrastructure
workAreas.focus: Global Edge caching (Cloudflare), database read-replica scaling, auto-scaling Kubernetes nodes, and multi-region failover.
workAreas.targets: 99.99% storefront uptime during flash sales, sub-50ms edge cache hits, sub-5min failover.

targets.primarySla: 99.99% storefront & checkout availability with sub-800ms checkout response times
targets.qualityStandard: Zero checkout drop-off bugs, 85%+ test coverage, validated 100k concurrent user peak resilience
targets.sprintVelocity: Weekly feature and promotional releases with zero regressions and verified payment logs
targets.etaDiscipline: All store features and bug fixes require developer ETA commitment before start; proactive manager follow-ups

featureDevelopment.title: E-Commerce Feature & Storefront Release Pipeline
steps: 1. Intake & Scoping: Promotional campaign or checkout feature requested by Merchandising or Commercial leadership.
2. Triage & Technical Review: E-Commerce Operations Manager reviews API specifications, evaluates conversion impact, and approves ticket.
3. Developer Assignment: Manager assigns the feature ticket to the designated storefront or inventory developer via delegate_task.
4. Mandatory ETA Request: Manager requests a concrete Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) before frontend or backend implementation begins.
5. ETA Commitment & Tracking: Developer calculates scope, commits to an ETA, and logs milestones on the commercial sprint board.
6. Active Follow-Ups: If deliverables or code reviews stall past the ETA, Manager immediately follows up, removes API blockers, and secures launch date.
7. Implementation & Testing: Developer writes modular code following Next.js/React best practices, adds unit tests (85%+ coverage), and submits a PR.
8. Code Review & QA Handoff: Tech Lead checks for edge rendering performance; approved PR transitions to QA.

9. QA Verification Gate: QA executes automated Playwright checkout tests across mobile and desktop viewports. If payment flow fails, QA files bug report with repro steps; if passed, release sign-off is granted.
10. Production Deployment: SRE Lead verifies edge cache invalidation rules and deploys to global production clusters.

bugTriageAndResolution.title: E-Commerce Checkout & Inventory Bug Resolution Lifecycle
steps: 1. Defect Discovery: Telemetry flags cart abandonment spike, payment gateway error rate, or inventory desync.
2. QA Defect Report: QA logs an emergency ticket with user session recordings, cart IDs, payload logs, and repro steps submitted to E-Commerce Manager.
3. Management Triage: Manager declares priority (P0 for broken checkout/payments), freezes non-essential tasks, and dispatches to senior developer.
4. Urgent ETA Request: Manager demands an immediate fix ETA (sub-30min for checkout incidents).
5. ETA Follow-Up: Manager monitors progress continuously; if ETA expires, escalates to CTO and invokes emergency rollback if needed.
6. Fix Implementation: Developer remedies race condition or payment webhook parsing, adding regression tests.
7. QA Re-Verification: QA executes test purchases with live sandbox cards to confirm flawless checkout completion.
8. Production Rollout: SRE deploys emergency hotfix and monitors real-time transaction completion metrics.

initialProjectOnboarding.title: First-Time E-Commerce Codebase Exploration & Architecture Protocol
steps: 1. CTO Architecture Discovery: CTO explores repository structure, cart schemas, checkout pipelines, payment gateways, and catalog databases.
2. Architecture Memorization: CTO commits verified store architecture, webhook secrets, and inventory sync endpoints into facts.md via manage_agent_memory.
3. Module Partitioning: CTO divides codebase into Storefront UI, Cart & Checkout, Inventory ERP, and Fulfillment modules, delegating to Managers.
4. Managerial Decomposition: E-Commerce Operations Manager inspects module directories, records deployment recipes into procedural.md, and assigns tasks.
5. Developer Deep-Dive: Developers inspect assigned components, test local payment mock servers, and verify build configurations.
6. Universal Memory Commitment: All engineers record verified API endpoints, tax calculation rules, and shipping carrier schemas into facts.md and procedural.md.

leadershipRules.title: Strict E-Commerce Leadership Fidelity & Separation of Concerns
rules: CTO and Commercial/Operations Managers NEVER write frontend code, edit database records, or configure gateway keys directly.
Management coordinates campaign launches, assigns tickets, enforces ETA commitments, and removes technical impediments.
When asked to write code, leadership explains the enterprise retail hierarchy and immediately delegates downward using delegate_task.
